items.stem: Which of the following best describes "B2B commerce"?
items.answer: E-business in which both the parties are business firms.
items.markingKey: (b) B2B commerce: E-business in which both the parties are business firms.
options: E-business in which consumers sell to other consumers, usually through a website.
E-business in which both the parties are business firms.
Use of electronic networks for interactions among departments and people within the same firm.
Conduct of industry, trade and commerce using computer networks such as the internet.

items.stem: State one difference between traditional business and e-business on the basis of shape of organisation.
items.answer: traditional business: vertical or tall; e-business: horizontal or flat
items.markingKey: 1 mark: traditional business: vertical or tall; e-business: horizontal or flat

items.stem: Explain the following limitations of e-business: (i) Need for technology capability and competence (ii) Low personal touch.
items.answer: (i) Need for technology capability and competence: All parties must be comfortable with computers and the internet. (ii) Low personal touch: Online dealings lack face-to-face contact.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) All parties must be comfortable with computers and the internet. (ii) Online dealings lack face-to-face contact.

items.stem: Arjun orders groceries at midnight from an app. Which benefit or limitation of e-business is illustrated?
items.answer: Convenience
items.markingKey: (b) Convenience. E-business is available round the clock.
options: Incongruence between order taking and delivery speed
Ease of formation and lower investment

items.stem: Imran placed an online order in seconds but the goods took a week to arrive. Which benefit or limitation of e-business is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Incongruence between order taking and delivery speed. Information moves fast but goods take time.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Incongruence between order taking and delivery speed; 2 marks for the justification: Information moves fast but goods take time.

items.stem:
Vihaan runs a traditional stationery shop in Ranchi. His son suggests selling online too, because customers now order from home.
(i) Give two benefits Vihaan would gain from going online. (ii) Give two limitations he must be prepared for.
items.answer: (i) Global reach, convenience (24 x 7), lower cost of operation, speed (any two). (ii) Low personal touch, delay between order and delivery, transaction risk, need for technical skills (any two).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Global reach, convenience (24 x 7), lower cost of operation, speed (any two). (ii) Low personal touch, delay between order and delivery, transaction risk, need for technical skills (any two).

items.stem: A bank sends account statements and offers to customers by email. Which type of e-business is it? Justify your answer.
items.answer: B2C commerce. A firm interacts with consumers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying B2C commerce; 2 marks for the justification: A firm interacts with consumers.

items.stem: Which e-business term is described here? "E-business in which a business firm deals with consumers."
items.answer: B2C commerce
items.markingKey: (b) B2C commerce: E-business in which a business firm deals with consumers.

items.stem: Zoya started an online store from home without renting a shop. Which benefit or limitation of e-business is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Ease of formation and lower investment. No large investment in physical premises is needed.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Ease of formation and lower investment; 2 marks for the justification: No large investment in physical premises is needed.

items.stem:
Bose Retail is deciding whether to open ten new showrooms or build an online store. Its products are standardised branded furniture.
(i) Compare the two on cost of setting up, global reach and response time. (ii) Which would you recommend and why? (iii) Name one risk it must guard against.
items.answer: (i) Online: lower cost, global reach, instantaneous response; showrooms: high cost, local reach, slower response. (ii) Online store (perhaps with a few showrooms): standardised branded goods need little trial, so online selling suits them. (iii) Transaction risk or data security risk such as hacking.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Online: lower cost, global reach, instantaneous response; showrooms: high cost, local reach, slower response. (ii) Online store (perhaps with a few showrooms): standardised branded goods need little trial, so online selling suits them. (iii) Transaction risk or data security risk such as hacking.

items.stem: Which of the following is true of traditional business but not of e-business?
items.answer: Cost of setting up: high
items.markingKey: (d) traditional business: Cost of setting up: high. The other options describe e-business.
options: Shape of organisation: horizontal or flat

items.stem: Distinguish between traditional business and e-business on the basis of physical presence, internal communication and product trial before purchase.
items.answer: (i) Physical presence: traditional business: required; e-business: not required. (ii) Internal communication: traditional business: hierarchical; e-business: non-hierarchical, vertical, horizontal or diagonal. (iii) Product trial before purchase: traditional business: possible; e-business: not possible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Physical presence: traditional business: required; e-business: not required. (ii) Internal communication: traditional business: hierarchical; e-business: non-hierarchical, vertical, horizontal or diagonal. (iii) Product trial before purchase: traditional business: possible; e-business: not possible.

items.answer: (i) Secure websites for payment: Card details are entered only on secure payment pages. (ii) Verifying the identity of parties: Reduces default and fraud due to anonymity.

items.stem:

items.answer: (i) Transaction risk (default on payment) and data storage and transmission risk. (ii) Cash on delivery; encryption, passwords and antivirus or firewall (any one).

items.answer: (i) Registration, placing the order in a shopping cart, payment, delivery. (ii) Cash on delivery, net banking transfer, credit or debit card (also cheque, digital cash). (iii) Encryption of data on secure payment pages.
